How rankings work
Source ingestion — Raw values from KeepTradeCut Crowd SF-TE++, KeepTradeCut Trades SF-TE++, IDP Trade Calculator, Dynasty League Football Superflex, Dynasty League Football Rookie SF, Dynasty League Football IDP, Dynasty League Football Rookie IDP, The IDP Show — Combined (Adamidp), Dynasty Nerds SF-TEP, FantasyCalc Dynasty SF, OTC Fantasy Football SF, Fantasy Navigator SF, Play for Keeps Dynasty, Dynasty Daddy Superflex, FantasyPros Dynasty Superflex, FantasyPros Dynasty IDP, FantasyPros / Pat Fitzmaurice SF-TEP, Flock Fantasy Superflex, Flock Fantasy Rookie SF, Yahoo / Justin Boone SF-TEP, Draft Sharks Dynasty, Draft Sharks IDP Dynasty.
Per-source ranking — Each player ranked within each source by raw value (highest = rank 1).
Rank normalization — Per-source ranks converted to 1–9,999 values via Hill-curve formula so sources are comparable.
Blended ranking — Multi-source players get averaged normalized values. Single-source players keep their one value.
Unified sort — All players sorted by blended value into one board. Top 800 get a consensus rank.
Tier detection — Natural value clusters detected via gap analysis. Tier breaks appear where adjacent players have unusually large value gaps.
Confidence scoring — multi-source agreement, measured on the backend’s spread signal.
Identity validation — Post-ranking pass checks for entity resolution problems. Flagged rows are quarantined (confidence degraded, not removed).
Hill curve (percentile form, scope masters): p = clamp((rank-1)/(referenceN-1), 0, 1); value = clamp(9999/(1 + (p/c)^s), 1, 9999) (referenceN = 500)
